note: The benchmark page's views (benchmark-views ticket 05): one tab per kind of job the user picks a Lane for, each a set of score/cost plots, one per board. `boards` lists [source, benchmark] pairs in plot order; a benchmark name also matches a versioned one (`Terminal-Bench` matches `Terminal-Bench 2.1`) and the newest version is drawn, so a new version of a board needs no edit here. A pair no board answers is left out. `reference` marks a composite view: it is drawn, never weighed against the job views. `why` is curated, says what decision the view helps with, and is not the source's claim; the source's own words are in boards.json. No model, harness or effort is named here: which Lanes a view lists is the catalog's, found at runtime.

views.title: Coding
views.why: An agent writing and operating code: terminal tasks end to end, and whole-repository moves checked by the repository's own tests. The closest boards to a delegated coding job.

views.title: Knowledge work
views.why: Professional deliverables graded against an expert's, whether a model knows the answer or says it does not, reasoning over long documents, and hard science questions. Research, review and writing jobs lean on these.

views.title: Automation
views.why: Multi-step business workflows driven through APIs, and following precise instructions. Evidence for tool-calling jobs, not for clicking through a browser.

views.title: Overall
views.why: One composite across agents, coding, reasoning and knowledge. A first cut for reference, never the whole answer.
